newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies following several interventions by the Bank of Israel, dealers said.

"The basket was trading today at 7.1 percent below the slope and the Bank of Israel had to intervene several times in the market by buying dollars to support the basket," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi.
"Despite the fact that the Bank of Israel intervened on a relatively high scale the basket traded after the setting of the representative rate at 7.01 percent below the slope," he said.

The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1530 against 3.1470 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5442 shekels against 3.5430 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8933 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8812 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1135 shekels per mark against 2.1205 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1525 shekels.
